posts.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
posts.description: I loved Blade Runner, both the 1982 original and the 2017 sequel. So this book, the one they’re both based on, has been on my list for a long while. I’m very happy I finally got around to it. On the surface it’s a story about the people left on Earth after World War Terminus. Rick Deckard is a bounty hunter who “retires” outlaw androids, and he’s handed six that have just escaped.

posts.title: The Death of Grass
posts.description: I was in the mood for a post-apocalyptic story, and John Christopher delivered, above and beyond. No zombies, though. No mushroom cloud. Just a virus that kills grass — all of it, rice and wheat and barley included. The threat isn’t out there waiting to attack. It’s the slow realization that food is finite and running out, and that everyone else has realized it too.

posts.title: Discover Your Message
posts.description: I picked this up wanting a straight answer to a practical question: how do you figure out what your message should be, to build your personal brand around? What I got was a motivational speech. My gut told me to bail after the first few pages, and I should have listened.
